Angle the torso slightly; keep the blue coat distinct from the black underlayers with controlled fill.\n\n15:30 — **Coat-silhouette profile.** Shoot through 16:00 with the high collar and structured shoulders outlined against a clean background. Use a slow pivot for restrained coat movement; keep the safe cosplay sword lowered and clear of the legs.\n\n16:00 — **Diagonal-blade portrait.** Shoot through 16:30, echoing the reference’s sword diagonal without crossing the eyes. Adjust blade angle to manage reflections; preserve the contrast between silver metal, blue fabric, and the reserved face.\n\n16:30 — **Controlled walking frame.** Shoot through 17:00 with short, deliberate steps that open the coat enough to reveal its dark lining. Maintain prop clearance and avoid exaggerated action poses.\n\n17:00 — **Face-and-collar close-up.** Shoot through 17:30, emphasizing swept-back silver hair, narrowed gaze, and blue collar texture. Add subtle side fill if needed; exclude distracting background details.\n\n17:30 — **Still final tableau.** Finish at 18:00 with a planted stance, settled coat, and sword held safely away from the body.\n\n**Weather contingency:** Move under shelter if rain starts or coat/prop control deteriorates. Tokyo’s precipitation probability is **30% at both 17:00 and 18:00**, with wind speeds of **13 kph at 17:00** and **12 kph at 18:00**; these warrant a backup, not an assumption of rain.","type":"response.output_text.done"}
